LESSON: METALLIC MATERIALS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Materials for Production
Topic 3.2: Metallic Materials
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Metallic Materials, part of Materials for Production in Grade 7 PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How are metallic materials used in day-to-day life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify types of metallic materials used in the immediate environment,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Metallic Materials in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. describe the physical properties of metallic materials found in the immediate environment,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Metallic Materials in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. relate metallic materials to their use in the immediate environment,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Metallic Materials in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the use of metallic materials in production.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Metallic Materials in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify types of metallic materials used in the immediate environment,

   Metallic Materials helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. describe the physical properties of metallic materials found in the immediate environment,

   Metallic Materials helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. relate metallic materials to their use in the immediate environment,

   Metallic Materials helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. appreciate the use of metallic materials in production.

   Metallic Materials helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. use print or digital media to search for information on metallic materials,

2. prepare a checklist for identifying types of metallic materials (steel, aluminium, copper),

3. perform practical activities to examine the physical properties of metallic materials (magnetism, conductivity of heat and electricity, appearance),

4. discuss the physical properties of metallic materials,

5. match metallic materials to their use in the immediate environment.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. use print or digital media to search for information on metallic materials,
2. prepare a checklist for identifying types of metallic materials (steel, aluminium, copper),
3. perform practical activities to examine the physical properties of metallic materials (magnetism, conductivity of heat and electricity, appearance),
4. discuss the physical properties of metallic materials,
5. match metallic materials to their use in the immediate environment.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Metallic Materials together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital Literacy: learner develops skills of interacting with technology when searching for information on metallic materials.

• Communication and Collaboration: learner acquires speaking, listening, and teamwork skills when discussing the uses of

metallic materials.

18

Values:
• Unity: learner displays team spirit and collaboration with others while discussing the uses of metallic materials.

• Responsibility: learner shows accountability by caring for the print or digital media when searching for information on

metallic materials.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Peer Education and Mentorship: the learner develops inter-personal relationships when performing practical activities to

examine the physical properties of metallic materials.

Link to other Subjects:

Integrated Science: learner enhances knowledge on properties of materials during discussion of physical properties of metallic

materials.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. identify types of metallic materials used in the immediate environment,
2. describe the physical properties of metallic materials found in the immediate environment,
3. relate metallic materials to their use in the immediate environment,
4. appreciate the use of metallic materials in production.

Remember the key question: How are metallic materials used in day-to-day life?
